title: Belief Systems, Ideologies and Worldviews
summary: Major religions and belief systems in South Africa, ideologies and worldviews, how beliefs shape values and behaviour, freedom of religion, and respecting diversity.

items: **Religion**: a set of beliefs, practices and rituals related to the sacred or divine (e.g. Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Judaism, African Traditional Religion).
**Worldview**: a person's overall view of the world, including beliefs about life, humanity and morality. It may be religious or secular (non-religious).
**Ideology**: a set of ideas about how society should be organised (e.g. democracy, capitalism, socialism, ubuntu as a social philosophy).

notes.title: Belief, ideology or worldview?
notes.problem: Identify: (a) 'I believe in ancestors.' (b) Capitalism. (c) A person's whole way of seeing life.
steps: (b) A political or economic system of ideas: ideology.

rows: Belief in God and Jesus Christ; the Bible; churches; Christmas and Easter
Belief in one God (Allah) and the Prophet Muhammad; the Qur'an; five pillars including prayer and fasting during Ramadan
Many forms of the divine; karma and reincarnation; festivals such as Diwali
Belief in one God; the Torah; the Sabbath; Passover
Belief in a Supreme Being and the ancestors; rituals and ceremonies; strong community ties
Ethics based on reason and human well-being rather than religion

notes.label: Ubuntu
notes.text: *Umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu*: 'a person is a person through other people'. Ubuntu emphasises compassion, respect and community, and is shared across many South African cultures and belief systems.

Section 15 of the Constitution protects freedom of **conscience, religion, thought, belief and opinion**. Public schools may hold religious observances if they are fair, voluntary and follow rules set by the school governing body. No one may be unfairly discriminated against because of religion (section 9).

items: Learn about other beliefs from reliable sources and respectful questions.
Avoid stereotypes and jokes that mock beliefs.
Focus on shared values: kindness, honesty, justice and caring for others.
Respect people's right to hold different beliefs, or none.

notes.title: Handling a clash of beliefs
notes.problem: A learner needs time off for a religious festival. How should a school respond?
steps: Section 15 of the Constitution protects freedom of religion.
The school should listen and reasonably accommodate the learner.
notes.answer: Accommodate the request, respecting religious freedom.
